properties.areaDesc: South Slopes Of The Central Brooks Range
properties.headline: Winter Storm Warning issued October 23 at 11:57PM AKDT until October 26 at 10:00PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Heavy snow expected. Total snow accumulations between 8 to
16 inches. Winds could gust as high as 35 mph.

* WHERE...South Slopes of the Central Brooks Range.

* WHEN...From 10 AM Saturday to 10 PM AKDT Monday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The snow will come in two waves. The first
will be on Saturday morning into Sunday morning with accumulations
around 4 to 8 inches. There will be a break with lighter snow
Sunday afternoon through Sunday night. Heavier snow returns Monday
morning and continues into the evening with an additional 4 to 8
inches of snow.
properties.instruction:
If you must travel, keep an extra flashlight, food, and water in your
vehicle in case of an emergency. Visit 511.alaska.gov or call 5 1 1
for the latest road conditions.

NWSheadline: WINTER STORM WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT FROM 10 AM SATURDAY TO 10 PM AKDT MONDAY

properties.areaDesc: Upper Koyukuk Valley
properties.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued October 23 at 11:57PM AKDT until October 26 at 10:00PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Snow expected. Total snow accumulations between 5 and 10
inches and a glaze of ice. Winds gusting as high as 30 mph.

* WHERE...Upper Koyukuk Valley.

* WHEN...From 10 AM Saturday to 10 PM AKDT Monday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The snow will come in two waves. Snow is more
likely Saturday morning into Sunday morning with 3 to 6 inches
expected. There will be a break with lighter snow Sunday afternoon
and night. On Monday, snow is likely in the morning with 2 to 4
inches expected but rain becomes more likely in the afternoon as
warmer temperatures intrude and this will limit snowfall totals.
Any rain will act as freezing rain and accrete on surfaces below
freezing. This could make for slick conditions early next week.
properties.instruction: Slow down and use caution while traveling.

properties.headline: Special Marine Warning issued October 24 at 3:50AM EDT until October 24 at 4:15AM EDT by NWS Key West FL
properties.description:
SMWKEY

The National Weather Service in Key West has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Gulf of America including Dry Tortugas and Rebecca Shoal Channel...
Straits of Florida from Halfmoon Shoal to 20 nm west of Dry
Tortugas out 20 nm...

* Until 415 AM EDT.

* At 350 AM EDT, a strong thunderstorm was located 8 nm west of
Tortugas Ecological Reserve South, moving south at 10 knots.

HAZARD...Wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...National Weather Service Meteorologist.

IMPACT...Expect wind gusts in excess of 34 knots, suddenly higher
waves, frequent lightning, and heavy downpours.

* The strong thunderstorm will remain over mainly open waters.
properties.instruction:
Prepare for wind gusts in excess of 34 knots, steep and fast-building
seas, frequent lightning, and blinding downpours. Stay low or go
below, and make sure all on board are wearing life jackets.

lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...New Kent, Gloucester, Eastern King William, Eastern
King and Queen and York Counties.

* WHEN...Until noon EDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Shallow flooding is expected in the most vulnerable
locations near the waterfront and shoreline resulting in a low
threat of property damage. Expect up to one foot of water
above ground level in low lying, vulnerable areas. Some roads
and low lying property including parking lots, parks and lawns
near the waterfront will experience shallow flooding.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.
